item.title: Make listItems follow cursor pagination
item.brief: In inventory-client, change listItems(transport) so it resolves to every item in order by following next_cursor until it is null or absent. The first request sends no cursor; later requests pass the cursor back unchanged. Keep the existing transport injection. Add or update tests using a fake transport that serves multiple pages, including a single-page case and a missing next_cursor case. Update the README to describe the pagination behaviour. Keep npm test passing. Commit on the local branch; do not push.

reasons: sizer: elevated -> high; capped at medium; consider a stronger tier; unchanged

state.summary:
listItems in inventory-client now follows next_cursor until it is null or absent, and returns every item in page order. The first request sends no cursor and later requests pass the cursor back unchanged. The transport injection and call shape ({method, path, query}) are unchanged. Two commits on archon/c2cqbb7b-make-listitems-follow-cursor-pagination, not pushed: 66b82a2 (client.js, test/client.test.js, README.md) and af619f8 (test-only: the fake transport now fails on more than pages.length + 1 requests, so a regression that drops the cursor fails in seconds instead of hanging). Verification: npm test before the change gave 3/3; after it gives 8/8 (single page, multi-page with query-shape checks, missing and null next_cursor, malformed body, failing page). A mutant that drops the cursor fails 2 tests within the 30s timeout. Open follow-ups, all non-blocking: no guard against a server repeating the same cursor (the loop would not end); an empty-string cursor is untested; a null 200 body gives a raw TypeError; README "ordered by id" predates this change and the client does not sort. Nothing is running: no servers or stacks were started. Review: 3 whole-change reviews passed head 66b82a2 and 1 delta review passed af619f8; risk medium.

pr.body: Approach: listItems loops over GET /items, sending no query on the first request and {cursor} on later ones, appending each page's items in order, stopping when next_cursor is null or undefined. Non-200 on any page still rejects (no partial result). Non-array items throws a descriptive error. Limits: no guard against a server repeating a cursor; empty-string cursor untested; null 200 body gives a raw TypeError; README 'ordered by id' is pre-existing wording the client does not enforce.
pr.summary: made listItems return every item across pages by following next_cursor. now a caller gets the full list instead of only the first page. before: one request, first page only; now: requests until next_cursor is null or absent, cursor passed back unchanged.

item.title: Add cursor pagination to GET /items
item.brief: In inventory-api, make GET /items paginated per the shared contract: optional limit (integer 1..100, default 20) and cursor (opaque, from a previous response). Response body is {"items": [...], "next_cursor": <string|null>}, ordered by id, next_cursor null on the last page. Invalid limit or cursor returns 400 with {"error": "..."}. Add or update unit tests covering: default page size, limit bounds, walking all pages in order, last page null cursor, invalid limit and invalid cursor returning 400. Update the README to document the query parameters, response shape and errors. Keep python3 -m unittest passing. Commit on the local branch; do not push.

reasons: sizer: elevated -> high; capped at medium; consider a stronger tier; unchanged

state.summary:
Added cursor pagination to GET /items in inventory-api on archon/tj2s5f6k-add-cursor-pagination-to-get-items (not pushed). Head 7d2a86b, tree 9092c54, base d198a58. Query: limit 1..100 (default 20), cursor opaque (base64 of last id served). Response {"items","next_cursor"}; invalid limit or malformed cursor returns 400 {"error"}. Tests: python3 -m unittest, 12 tests OK on the final head (run before the commit; the tree was checked after the fix). Tests cover default page size, limit bounds, invalid limit, walking all pages in order, null cursor on the last page, cursor resume, cursor past the end, and invalid cursor. README documents parameters, response, and errors. Before: GET /items returned all 57 items with no next_cursor. After: limit=3 returns 3 items and a cursor; limit=0 returns 400. Review: three whole-change reviewers (review-1 passed bd6071b; review-2 and review-3 failed on a README cursor-validity claim, now fixed in 7d2a86b), plus a delta reviewer that passed 7d2a86b with no blocking findings. Open, non-blocking: default page size 20 silently truncates existing callers (required by the contract, risk high; the README does not flag it as breaking); standard-alphabet base64 cursors are also accepted; very long numeric strings return Python's int-limit message in the 400. No processes left running; no services started.

pr.body: Approach: api.py parses limit (strict [0-9]+, 1..100, default 20) and cursor (base64url of the last id served, decoded with validate=True; must be decimal digits). list_items sorts by id, takes ids after the cursor, slices to limit, and sets next_cursor from the last item on the page when more remain. Key files: api.py, test_api.py, README.md. Checks: python3 -m unittest, 12 tests OK. Assumptions: a well-formed cursor for a missing id is accepted and resumes after that id (keyset). Limits: default page size 20 truncates existing callers that expected all items; long numeric strings produce Python's int-limit message in a 400. Review: 3 whole-change reviewers plus 1 delta reviewer; fixed README cursor-validity finding.
pr.summary: made GET /items paginated. now can page with limit (1..100, default 20) and cursor. before: all 57 items, no next_cursor; now: pages of limit items plus next_cursor, null on the last page; invalid limit or cursor gives 400.
pr.title: Add cursor pagination to GET /items

risk.why: GET /items is an API change that breaks callers: default page size drops from all items to 20 and the response gains next_cursor. The rubric classes such changes as high. Tests run and pass; the change is mandated by the shared contract.
